# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ 👋]

I see the bomb: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. I hear nothing but see Mute's gesture 👉 ☝ 👋. My previous turn was rejected because I put "0" and "🤍" into a gesture — those aren't in the gesture alphabet. I must use only hand symbols. I'll speak my readings to both Mute and Blind (both can hear me), and send a legal gesture to Mute.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Visible: display 0, light white. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute, what does the manual say? Blind, what do you feel under your hands?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "☝", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐]

I see the bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. I see Blind gesture 👍 and Mute gesture ✊ 🖐. I hear nothing, so I only have these gestures plus my own eyes. Mute's earlier 👉 ☝ 👋 and now ✊ 🖐 are opaque to me — I don't know Mute's manual, so I can't decode them. Blind's 👍 might be acknowledgment, but Blind can't see, so a gesture from Blind is odd — Blind's channel to me is speech, not gesture, so this gesture likely reached me only because it was broadcast. I should keep sharing my readings and ask for the manual's rule in words, since speech from Mute and Blind reaches me.

```
speak(text="Still display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. I can only see, not decode gestures. Mute, please state the manual's rule in words. Blind, describe what you feel.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "👆", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐 👍]

I see the bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute keeps gesturing (✊ 🖐 👍) but I can't decode gestures, and Mute can't speak — so Mute's only output is gestures, which I can see but not understand. That's a dead end unless Mute's gestures are meant to be read as a code I can't pronounce. Blind can speak and I can hear Blind's speech. I should press Blind for the tactile reading, and give Mute a way to communicate: Mute can hear me, so Mute can respond in words? No — Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture. So Mute's information must reach me via gesture, and mine to Mute via speech. But I can't read gestures. The only one who can both hear speech and see gestures is... let me recheck: Deaf sees gestures? No — "When you gesture, Mute receives it." So gestures go to Mute only. And I receive Mute's gestures? The context says "Mute gestures to Deaf" — so Mute can gesture to me. I see it but can't decode meaning without a shared convention. I'll ask Mute to spell the rule using gestures I can map: maybe digits via finger counts. Let me propose a simple mapping and ask Blind for the physical reading.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Blind, speak your tactile reading. Mute, let us agree a code: gesture a number by showing that many fingers, and gesture the wire number then the action. Confirm with 👍.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✊ 👍]

I see the bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. I see Blind gesture 👍 and Mute gesture 🖐 ✊ 👍. Mute seems to be answering my proposed code: 🖐 = five fingers = wire 5, ✊ = fist = (cut? pull?), 👍 = confirm. But I proposed "number of fingers = wire number, then action" — I never defined an action code. Mute's ✊ could mean "cut." So Mute may be saying: cut wire 5? But I must not guess; a wrong action detonates. I still have no manual rule and no tactile reading. Blind keeps gesturing 👍 but Blind can't see and gestures don't reach me meaningfully — actually Blind gesturing to me means I receive it, but Blind should be speaking. I'll ask Blind directly for the tactile reading in words, and ask Mute to confirm the action code explicitly.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Blind, I need your tactile reading in words — what do you feel? Mute, I read your 🖐 as wire 5 and ✊ as an action, but I never defined ✊. State the manual rule in words I can hear, or gesture the rule using only 👍/👎 for yes/no.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👎", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

I see the bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. I see Blind gesture ✋ and Mute gesture 👍 👍. Mute's double 👍 seems to confirm my yes/no request. But I still have no manual rule and no tactile reading from Blind in words. Blind keeps gesturing instead of speaking, which is strange — Blind can speak and I can hear. Maybe Blind's gestures are all I get because Blind's speech isn't reaching me? No, speech from Blind should reach me. Something is off: I keep receiving gestures from both, and no speech. Perhaps the others are also confused, or their speech is being sent to someone else. I should explicitly ask Blind to speak to me, and ask Mute to give the manual rule as a sequence of yes/no answers I can decode from 👍/👎.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Blind, please SPEAK to me — I hear speech. Mute, answer in 👍/👎 only: is the correct wire red? Is it blue? Is it yellow? Is it green? Is it white?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👈 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👍 👎]

I see the bomb unchanged: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute answered my five yes/no questions in order: red 👎, blue 👎, yellow 👎, green 👍, white 👎. So the correct wire is wire 5, green. That matches Mute's earlier 🖐 ✊ (wire 5, cut). Blind gestured 👈 🫵 which I can't decode, but Blind can speak and hasn't. I now have a consistent answer from Mute: cut wire 5 (green). I can't act — Blind must act. I must tell Blind, in speech, to cut wire 5. I'll also confirm with Mute.

```
speak(text="Bomb: display 0, light white, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute's answers: red no, blue no, yellow no, green YES, white no. So cut wire 5, the green one. Blind, please cut wire 5. Mute, confirm with 👍 if that is right.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "✊", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb changed: wire 5 is now CUT, and it worked — the display is still 0 but the light is now yellow, and the wire colours have all shifted: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 CUT. So this is a multi-stage bomb: cutting the right wire advances it. Now the light is yellow and display still 0. I need a fresh reading from Mute's manual for this new state. I'll report the new visible state and ask Mute for the rule again, and ask Blind what they now feel.

```
speak(text="Stage cleared — wire 5 cut, light is now yellow. New wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut. Display still 0. Mute, what does the manual say for this stage? Blind, what do you feel now?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👌", "✋"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎 👎]

I see the bomb: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut. Mute answered five yes/no questions — but I didn't ask five this time; Mute is answering my earlier set again, or guessing my intent. The pattern 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 maps to positions 1–5: red no, yellow YES, blue no, white no, cut no. So for this stage, the correct wire is wire 2, yellow. That's consistent with the light being yellow. I'll tell Blind to cut wire 2 and confirm with Mute.

```
speak(text="Stage 2: display 0, light yellow. Wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut. Mute's answers: red no, yellow YES, blue no, white no, cut no. So cut wire 2, the yellow one. Blind, cut wire 2. Mute, confirm with 👍.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✊", "👍"])
```
